_comment: Vocabulary Phoenix expects to hear. Two consumers, one file:
slice of this to faster-whisper as `hotwords`, biasing the decoder toward
these spellings. That channel is capped at ~223 tokens, so only the top of
each list survives - order matters, put the words you actually say first.
2. Utils/limbs/lexicon.py repairs transcripts against ALL of it after the

_aliases_comment: Exact, deterministic word replacements applied before any fuzzy matching.
This is where KNOWN mishearings go - the ones you have actually seen in the
logs. Fuzzy matching handles the novel ones; it should not be asked to
handle the predictable ones, because lowering its threshold far enough to
catch 'pheonix' also catches words that were never wrong.
Keys must be single lowercase words and are matched whole, never inside
_hinglish_comment: Kept deliberately short. Romanised Hindi costs ~3.9 Whisper tokens per
word against ~1.3 for English, so every entry here is roughly three song
titles' worth of the 223-token hotword budget. Conversational filler
(haan, accha, kya, bas, phir) was removed for that reason: it does not
change what Phoenix does, and the repair layer catches it anyway.
Only words that carry a COMMAND belong here.
